about.title: What is Mexican Loteria? History and Tradition | chorroybuenas.com.mx
about.metaDescription: Discover the history, culture and tradition behind Mexican Loteria. Learn about its origins and how it has united communities for generations.

hero.title: What is Mexican Lotería?
hero.description: A game of chance similar to bingo, but with pictures, verses and lots of togetherness. It has been part of Mexican celebrations for generations.

history.title: History and origin
history.intro: Lotería has its roots in Europe and was adapted in Mexico until it became a game of our own.

europe.title: Italy and Europe
europe.text: Its best-known ancestor is the Italian “lotto”, a game of chance with numbers that spread through Europe and reached Spain.

colonial.title: Colonial era
colonial.text: With the Spanish, the game arrived in New Spain. At first it was a pastime of the wealthy; over time it became part of town fairs and festivities.

mexican.title: It becomes Mexican
mexican.text: Numbers were replaced by pictures of daily life and popular culture: El Gallo, La Dama, El Catrín, La Sirena… In the late 19th century the 54-card deck that almost all of Mexico recognizes today became popular.

today.title: Today
today.text: It is played at fairs, kermeses, posadas and family gatherings; it is used in schools to learn words and even inspires art and design. And now you can also play it with your own photos.

history.sheetLabel: Lotería sheet with nine classic cards

culture.title: More than a game, a tradition
culture.text: Lotería has brought families and communities together for generations. It is learned from grandparents, played at parties and passed from parents to children, with the same shouts, the same laughter and the same beans.

deck.title: The 54 cards of traditional lotería
deck.intro: These are the names of the classic deck, in order. Each card has its number, its picture and, almost always, a verse the caller recites when drawing it.
deck.cardsLabel: The first twelve cards of the deck

what.question: What is Mexican lotería?
what.answer: It is a traditional game of chance, similar to bingo, but with pictures instead of numbers. A caller draws cards from a deck and players mark on their board the ones that come up.

bingo.question: What is the difference between lotería and bingo?
bingo.answer: In bingo numbers are called; in lotería, named pictures, often with a verse. Lotería also has its own plays such as el chorro, el centro or the four corners.

cards.question: How many cards does lotería have?
cards.answer: The traditional deck has 54 cards and each board has 16 pictures in a 4×4 grid.

origin.question: Where does lotería come from?
origin.answer: Its ancestor is the Italian “lotto”, which arrived in Mexico during the colonial era and here became the picture game we know.

own.question: Can I make a lotería with my own photos?
own.answer: Yes. On chorroybuenas you upload your photos, they become cards and you generate the boards and the deck in a print-ready PDF, for free.

cta.title: Ready to make your own lotería?
cta.text: Customize your game with your pictures and enjoy this Mexican tradition.

howToPlay.title: How to play Mexican Loteria? - Step-by-Step Instructions | chorroybuenas.com.mx
howToPlay.metaDescription: Learn how to play Mexican Loteria step by step. Clear instructions to prepare the game, call the cards and win. Have fun with tradition!

hero.title: How do you play Mexican Lotería?
hero.description: It is easy: a caller, boards, the deck and some beans. Here we explain everything in five minutes.
hero.imageAlt: Family playing lotería with printed boards and beans

boards.title: Boards
boards.text: One per player (or several, if you want more luck).

deck.title: The deck
deck.text: The cards cut out, shuffled and face down.

beans.title: Beans
beans.text: Or pebbles, coins or chips to mark with.

caller.title: A caller
caller.text: Draws the cards and announces them out loud.

deal.title: Hand out the boards
deal.text: Each player picks one or more boards. If there is a bet, everyone puts in their share per board and the pot is gathered.

draw.title: The caller draws a card
draw.text: They announce it by name, or with a verse or riddle to make it more fun.

mark.title: Mark it if you have it
mark.text: If the card is on your board, put a bean on it. Pay attention: the caller does not wait.

shout.title: Shout when you complete a play!
shout.text: When you complete the agreed play, shout its name. Your cards are checked and, if all is right, you take the prize.

calling.title: How to call the cards
calling.text1: The caller is the soul of the game. Instead of just saying the name of the card, the tradition is to announce it with a verse, a saying or a riddle, so players have to stay alert.
calling.text2: Many callers start each round with “¡Se va y se corre!”. With your own cards you can make up verses about each person: it is the part that gets the most laughs.

gallo.name: El Gallo
gallo.verse: «El que le cantó a San Pedro no le volverá a cantar.»

dama.name: La Dama
dama.verse: «Puliendo el paso, por toda la calle real.»

sirena.name: La Sirena
sirena.verse: «Con los cantos de sirena, no te vayas a marear.»

diablito.name: El Diablito
diablito.verse: «Pórtate bien, cuatito, si no te lleva el coloradito.»

plays.title: Plays and prizes
plays.intro: Before starting, agree on which plays count. The first person to complete a play takes it; after that, that play is closed.

chorro.title: El Chorro
chorro.text: A full line: horizontal, vertical or diagonal.
chorro.boardAlt: 4×4 board with a full row marked with beans

centro.title: El Centro
centro.text: The 4 cards in the center of the board.
centro.boardAlt: 4×4 board with the four center cards marked with beans

esquinas.title: Las 4 Esquinas
esquinas.text: The cards in the four corners.
esquinas.boardAlt: 4×4 board with the four corners marked with beans

lleno.title: Tablero Lleno
lleno.text: Every card. It is the top prize and ends the round.
lleno.boardAlt: 4×4 board with every card marked with beans

plays.others: Some families add other plays, such as El Marco (the 12 cards on the edge) or La X (the two diagonals). What matters is agreeing before you start.

buenas.title: ¡Buenas!
buenas.text: In many homes, instead of “¡Lotería!”, people shout ¡Buenas! when they win. And when someone completes a line, it is a chorro! That is where our name comes from.

bet.title: What if we play for money?
bet.text: Everyone puts in an amount per board. What is gathered (the pot) is split among the plays: for example, one part for El Chorro, another for El Centro and the biggest for Tablero Lleno.

kids.title: Lotería for small children
kids.text: With 3×3 boards (9 pictures) rounds are shorter and easier to follow. For the little ones, it is best to play for a line or a full board, and to use cards they recognize: family, pets or favorite toys. On chorroybuenas you need at least {{kids}} cards to make Kids Mode boards.

howMany.title: How many boards do I need?
howMany.text: At least one per player, plus a few more for anyone who wants to play with two. The more cards the deck has, the more different the boards are and the fewer ties there are. On chorroybuenas, Classic Mode needs at least {{classic}} cards.

cards.question: How many cards does Mexican lotería have?
cards.answer: The traditional deck has 54 cards, each with its number, picture and name. A custom lotería can have as many as you want; on chorroybuenas the minimum is {{classic}} ({{kids}} in Kids Mode).

board.question: How many cards are on each board?
board.answer: In the traditional game, 16, arranged in 4 rows of 4. In Kids Mode, 9 (3×3).

chorro.question: What is the chorro in lotería?
chorro.answer: It is completing a line of cards: horizontal, vertical or diagonal. It is usually the first play won in each round.

shout.question: What do you shout when you win?
shout.answer: “¡Lotería!” or “¡Buenas!”, depending on each home. For the smaller plays you shout their name: “¡Chorro!”, “¡Centro!”, “¡Esquinas!”.

tie.question: What if two people win at the same time?
tie.answer: The most common thing is to split the prize between them. It is best to agree before you start.

markers.question: What do you mark the cards with?
markers.answer: Traditionally with beans, but pebbles, coins, chips or bottle caps work too.

about.title: Free printable traditional lotería boards
about.text: In Mexico many players have their lucky board: the one they build with their favorite cards and that, they say, makes them shout “¡Lotería!” more often. Here you can create yours with the classic 54 cards, from El Gallo to La Rana, with no repeated cards on a board. Build one or up to 50, download them as a PDF and play with your classic deck.

free.question: Is it free?
free.answer: Yes. Building your boards and downloading them as a PDF costs nothing.

howMany.question: How many boards can I make?
howMany.answer: Up to 50 per game. You can build them one by one or add them at random.

size.question: What size do they print?
size.answer: Each board comes on its own letter-size page, with guides to cut it out.

account.question: Do I need an account?
account.answer: No. Your boards are saved in this browser. If you sign in, they are also saved to your account so you can print them again.

deck.question: Can I use them with my deck?
deck.answer: Yes. They use the 54 traditional lotería cards, so they work with the deck you already have.

why.question: Why build my own board?
why.answer: Many people believe that playing with a board made of their favorite cards brings good luck. Plus, nobody else has one like it.
